container.title: How is a video built?
container.lead: A video is like a lunchbox: several things sit inside, each in its own place. Let's look inside.

box.heading: 1. The box
box.text: A video file is a container, a box. Several tracks sit inside: pictures, sound and often subtitles. Each track runs on its own, but they are all linked over time.

video.name: Picture track
video.text: Many pictures in a row. Videos often have 25 to 60 pictures every second.

audio.name: Sound track
audio.text: The sound is stored as a long row of numbers. There can also be several sound tracks, for example for different languages.

subtitles.name: Subtitle track
subtitles.text: Text with a start and an end time. Not every video has one.

info.name: Information
info.text: Length, size, pictures per second and the creation date. They apply to the whole video.

frames.heading: 2. The pictures and the sound
frames.text: The strip shows some pictures from the video. Drag the line with the mouse or your finger, or use the arrow keys. Below it you see the sound as a waveform: high peaks are loud spots.
frames.hint: Arrow keys: one picture. Page up and down: one second. Home and End: start and end.
frames.clip: A 2-second excerpt: 12 pictures, each 1/6 second long. The time axis, the pictures and the sound show the same 2 seconds.

endings.heading: 3. The ending is only the box
endings.text: The ending after the name, for example .mp4, only tells you which box it is. What is inside the box is a different question.

mp4.text: The most common box. Phones, school computers and websites can almost always open it.

webm.text: An open box that is often used for websites.

mov.text: Apple's box (QuickTime). Many phone videos from iPhones are stored this way.

mkv.text: A big box that can hold many tracks, for example several sound tracks.

endings.memo: The ending is the box. The codec is the packing method for the pictures and the sound. Both must fit your player.

app.heading: 4. How Jelly Cut reads the file
app.text: When you drag a video into the library, Jelly Cut reads the box on your computer: length, pictures per second and sound. The file is not uploaded. It stays where it is.
app.text2: If your browser cannot read a track or the packing method, Jelly Cut shows a message. Then a Chromium-based browser such as Brave, Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome will help.
app.tip: Jelly Cut only reads your file. Your original file stays unchanged.
